name: proposal-bound sensitive AI actions
evidenceBoundary: source, database, integration and development UI only

rootCauses.finding: Sensitive execution is authorized by confirmation words in the newest user message rather than an immutable proposal record.
The pending proposal is reconstructed from assistant tool-call JSON and AsyncLocalStorage instead of storage-enforced proposal identity.
Mutation classification is optional per tool definition; omitted metadata permits direct execution.
Several AI tools write directly through Prisma or duplicate provider workflows instead of one proposal-bound command executor.
Current confirmation does not bind actor, approver, device, session, exact shop, policy, permission, entitlement, target versions, expiry or one-time execution.
A response replay, duplicated approval request or restart can regenerate arguments or repeat a mutation because there is no unique proposal-to-execution claim.
The streaming UI confirms by sending the generic text 'oui', allowing Gemini to choose or regenerate the next function call.
The streaming route can deliver a mutation result before assistant-message persistence and silently swallow persistence failure; action truth must come from dedicated action records.

frozenContract.proposal: Gemini function-call arguments are validated, canonicalized, encrypted and persisted before the UI receives an approval request.
frozenContract.identity: Proposal digest binds tool, encrypted argument hash, request actor, session, device, workspace, installation, shop incarnation, registry revision, policy version, revocation epoch, required permissions, license projection, target versions and expiry.
frozenContract.approval: The approval endpoint receives only a proposal ID and decision. Server authority revalidates the stored digest, current approver, exact shop, permission, license, expiry and target versions.
frozenContract.execution: One unique execution row claims one proposal exactly once. Mutation replay returns the stored result and never regenerates arguments.
frozenContract.commands: Supported database mutations execute through canonical services inside a proposal-idempotent BusinessCommand. Provider effects are disabled unless an existing durable effect protocol can be reused without convergence work.
frozenContract.catalog: Every registered tool declares a central execution class. Unknown or unclassified tools fail closed and are not sent to Gemini.
frozenContract.history: UI reads sanitized proposal, approval and execution projections; encrypted arguments and raw result details never leave the server.
frozenContract.recovery: Expired, tampered, stale-policy, stale-entitlement, target-conflict and interrupted execution states are explicit and cannot be approved silently.

blockedSensitiveTools.name: assign_order_to_delivery
blockedSensitiveTools.reason: Courier/provider convergence is a Task 5 non-goal; the current AI tool duplicates provider execution and therefore must not be exposed for mutation.

requiredTests: proposal arguments are encrypted and digest-bound
actor, device, session and shop drift fail closed
permission, policy and entitlement drift fail closed
response replay returns one stored result
restart after execution claim does not repeat a mutation
sensitive tool direct invocation without sealed execution authority fails
unclassified mutation tools are not exposed
blocked provider mutation is not exposed
Arabic, French and English approval and stale/conflict states render with RTL-safe identifiers
